input.raw_text: Something structural has changed in how this market trades, and I keep coming back to the zero-day options. They are roughly half of SPX option volume now, and the intraday tape has acquired a mechanical quality I have not seen in twenty years. Mornings drift; then dealer hedging takes over and price accelerates toward the largest strike concentration, often snapping to round numbers before the close, then settling the moment expiry passes. Directionless most days, yet when a data print lands the move compresses into an hour of intensity because everyone trades the same expiry. Volatility sellers love it — realized vol stays low and the premium income prints — but risk is concentrating somewhere nobody stress-tested: a gap event with millions of contracts expiring that afternoon could force hedging one way with no natural buyers. The close-to-close tape looks calm, but the plumbing underneath is more leveraged than ever.
input.summary: Zero-day options account for roughly half of SPX option volume and appear to be making intraday price behavior more mechanical, with quiet mornings often giving way to dealer hedging flows toward concentrated strikes and round numbers before expiry. Most sessions remain directionless and realized volatility stays low, while data releases can compress price movement into a brief, intense interval. Calm close-to-close behavior may obscure concentrated gap-event risk, including potentially one-sided hedging demand amid limited natural buying interest.

interpretation.summary: Sustained low realized volatility weakly supports a depressed-volatility persistence state; the remaining candidates require behavior not observed at the relevant mechanism, horizon, or asset scope.

citations.text: GARCH(1,1) captures the empirical stylized fact of volatility clustering— large shocks followed by large shocks and small shocks followed by small shocks—through the GARCH persistence parameter delta. High persistence (delta close to 1) implies slow mean-reversion of conditional variance following a shock, producing extended periods of elevated or depressed volatility. Sections 1-2, p.1-6. Foundational motivation for GARCH in financial time series. The conditional variance h_t = omega + alpha*u_{t-1}^2 + delta*h_{t-1} dynamically adjusts to past shocks. When alpha+delta is near 1 (IGARCH), volatility shocks are near-permanent.

matched_states.evidence_caveats: Sustained subdued realized volatility supports the depressed-volatility persistence behavior, but shock-sequence clustering, squared-return autocorrelation, and GARCH persistence parameters are not measured.
matched_states.state_summary: A market condition characterized by persistent clustering of return volatility— large shocks followed by further large shocks and small shocks followed by further small shocks—captured by a GARCH(1,1) conditional variance process h_t = omega + alpha * u_{t-1}^2 + delta * h_{t-1}. High persistence (alpha + delta near 1, delta close to 1) implies slow mean-reversion of conditional variance following a shock, producing extended periods of elevated or depressed volatility. The state is active whenever GARCH persistence parameters are large and squared-return autocorrelations are significant.
matched_states.title: GARCH Volatility Clustering Persistence State
